body:
closes #68343

`IntervalArray.__new__` passed a `RangeIndex` or a non-interval ExtensionArray straight to the Cython `intervals_to_interval_bounds`. That function requires an ndarray, so users got `TypeError: Argument 'intervals' has incorrect type (expected numpy.ndarray, got ...)`. The reported case is a `RangeIndex`, which breaks `IntervalIndex` set ops with an empty `RangeIndex` (e.g. `pd.DataFrame().index`). The same error hits `pd.Index([], dtype="Int64").astype("interval")`, `pd.IntervalIndex(pd.Index(["a"]))`, and other masked, arrow, string, datetimelike and sparse inputs.

The fix extracts a `RangeIndex` to an ndarray and converts other non-interval EAs to ndarrays before the Cython call. Empty or all-NA input now builds an `IntervalIndex`, matching the numpy-backed equivalent; other input raises the usual "... is not an interval" error.

Unlike GH-68345, which special-cased `RangeIndex` in `_maybe_convert_platform_interval`, this fixes the constructor itself. That helper also serves `from_breaks`, which has to keep EA breaks intact.

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5.5 (high)`), which reproduced the bug, wrote the fix and tests, and ran the before/after comparison against main.
title: BUG: IntervalIndex raising Cython TypeError for RangeIndex and non-interval EA input (GH#68343)
